note: Both sets share the same core claims about the IR channel, guide channel, Saphira-based IFS detector, and coronagraphs, all supported by the page. B additionally captures two correct Table 5.5-4 facts for the UV Science channel (UV bandpass 0.2–0.45 µm and visible bandpass 0.45–0.67 µm, both marked science), which A omits entirely. Both sets repeat the guide-channel magnification claim verbatim, and both bind the 0.3–0.45 µm (guide) table entry to a somewhat generic 'Guide filter' entity. Otherwise the shared claims are faithful, with values, conditions and quotes matching the text and table.
remarks: Both sets state the guide-channel magnification ('32 pixels across the telescope aperture') twice. The table entry 0.3–0.45 µm (guide) sits in the IR Science column's UV bandpass row; labeling it 'Guide filter' is imprecise but not clearly wrong. Neither set extracts the visible/IR science bandpasses (0.45–1.0, 0.54–1.0, 1.6–1.8, 0.975–1.8 µm) or the fixed field stop's 4" value as a standalone quantity.
